kicker: Raon-1 nano, read from its headers

scenes.text: A model with 3.1B parameters that needs room for only half of them. Where does the other half go?
scenes.say: Here is a small language model with three point one billion parameters. On a phone, only about half of them need the fast memory. Where does the other half go?

scenes.headline: How Raon-1 nano keeps half its weights off the chip
scenes.sub: Per-layer embeddings, and a dense model cut from a mixture of experts
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Basalt! Today we open up Raon one nano, from KRAFTON, and count where every parameter lives.

scenes.title: Half is a lookup table
scenes.sub: Every token gets a private vector for every layer
scenes.say: Chapter one. Half is a lookup table.

steps.say: A normal model turns each token into one vector at the bottom of the stack, and that is the last time it consults the vocabulary.

steps.term: Per-layer embedding: a token vector for each layer
steps.say: Raon also keeps a second table, with one long row per token. The row is cut into twenty-four slices, one for each layer.
Each layer, after its attention and its feed-forward block, reads its own slice back in, through a gate that the hidden state controls.
The table holds one point six billion parameters. But a forward pass only ever fetches one row. It never multiplies by the rest.
Follow a single token through it.
The id selects one row of six thousand one hundred and forty-four numbers. At four bits, that is about three and a half kilobytes.
Each of the twenty-four layers takes its two hundred and fifty-six numbers, and multiplies them by a gate computed from the hidden state.
The result is projected back to full width and added to all four residual streams.

scenes.title: Where the bytes live
scenes.sub: Fast memory for what multiplies, slow memory for what is looked up
scenes.say: Chapter two. Where the bytes live.

scenes.title: Weights at 4-bit
scenes.say: At four bits, the weights every token multiplies come to about point eight six gigabytes. The table is another point nine, and it can stay in host memory or on flash.

left.title: Expanded keys and values
left.say: The reference PyTorch code expands its six attention caches to thirty-two full heads. That is about eighteen times too much for a phone.

right.title: Latent cache
right.say: Keep only the latent, and it is six thousand nine hundred and twelve bytes per token. The other eighteen layers keep a fixed state that never grows.

scenes.title: From experts to dense
scenes.sub: The paper behind the starting weights
scenes.say: Chapter three. From experts to dense.

scenes.title: MoE to dense, step by step

steps.say: Take one mixture of experts layer from Qwen three, with a hundred and twenty-eight experts and eight active per token. Score every expert on calibration text.

steps.term: D-optimal: pick the set with the most volume
steps.say: Keep eight. The best score multiplies importance by diversity, so the chosen experts do different work instead of repeating each other.
Stack the eight side by side, and they become one dense feed-forward block, six thousand one hundred and forty-four wide.
Then distil from the original mixture of experts, matching its output distribution.
The paper draws it like this. Experts are scored and chosen.
Then concatenated, and distilled with a K L loss from teacher to student.

scenes.title: After about 4B tokens of distillation
scenes.say: The paper's own result. After about four billion tokens, the diverse pick averages fifty-eight point one percent. Pruning a dense teacher of the same total size gets fifty-one point eight four.

scenes.title: Where nano departs from the paper
scenes.say: But Raon one nano is not that recipe, applied as written. Compare the two models side by side.

items.say: Its width is one thousand five hundred and thirty-six, not the teacher's two thousand five hundred and sixty.

items.text: A 1.6B table the teacher never had
items.say: It has a per-layer table that the teacher never had.
And it trained on three trillion more tokens. The paper never tests whether its head start survives that.

scenes.text: Parameters you look up are cheaper than parameters you multiply. Nano puts half its weights where only one row is ever read.
scenes.say: Parameters you look up are cheaper than parameters you multiply. Nano puts half its weights where only one row per token is ever read.

recap: Only compute weights need the fast memory
Diverse experts make a better dense start
scenes.say: To recap. Half the model is a lookup table. Only the weights that multiply need fast memory. And a diverse pick of experts is a better start than a pruned dense model.
